title: Define and Detect High-Quality Listings
prompt:
An Airbnb MLE interview report asks how to define and detect high-quality listings. It names retention, bad reviews, cancellations, disputes, refunds, and NPS as possible signals. Design a reliable quality measure and the evaluation loop around it.

Explain the quality definition, label horizon and leakage controls, data and modeling choices, validation, intervention, and monitoring. The report does not provide one canonical formula, horizon, or model: state any general preparation assumptions explicitly. This is a writing exercise.

response.placeholder: Begin with a time-bound, multi-objective definition of quality; do not collapse every reported outcome into an unexamined label.
response.reference_answer:
## Assumptions and target

Treat listing quality as a time-bound, multi-objective estimate of guest experience and transaction reliability, not as one universal score. As an exercise assumption, define outcome windows after a completed stay and keep the listed signals separate long enough to inspect their trade-offs. Retention, reviews, cancellations, disputes, refunds, and NPS are source-reported candidate signals, not a fixed formula.

## Labels and features

Build delayed labels from post-stay outcomes and freeze features as of the decision time. Exclude future reviews, support actions, and any information created after a booking from training inputs. Separate controllable listing attributes from request context and market conditions so a scarce market is not automatically judged low quality. Start with interpretable calibrated component scores or a multi-task model, using structured listing data plus permitted text or image features.

## Validation and use

Use time-based and market-held-out evaluation, then inspect calibration and error by listing age, geography, availability, and outcome completeness. A threshold should correspond to a concrete, reviewable action such as guidance, verification, or additional support; it should not silently become a permanent inventory-suppression rule. Test interventions against an appropriate control to distinguish score accuracy from the effect of acting on the score.

## Monitoring and safeguards

Monitor label delay, missingness, score drift, calibration, action rates, and downstream guest, host, and trust outcomes. Give new listings an uncertainty-aware fallback rather than treating no history as poor quality. Provide a review and appeal path, audit sensitive slices, and roll back an intervention when its guardrails worsen even if the headline score improves.
